A2. Interpretation cheatsheet

1. Aim

This appendix maps common output quantities to their estimands and valid one-sentence interpretations. Interpretations are conditional on coding, link, time origin, interaction structure, covariance estimator, and missing-data assumptions.

2. Model specification

\[ \text{GEE: }g\{E(Y_{ij})\}=x_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\beta_{PA}, \qquad \text{GLMM: }g\{E(Y_{ij}\mid b_i)\}=x_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\beta_{SS}+z_{ij}^{\mathsf T}b_i. \] For Gaussian LMMs, identity-link marginalization leaves \(\beta\) unchanged. For logistic random-intercept models, \(\beta_{PA}\approx\beta_{SS}/\sqrt{1+0.35\sigma_b^2}\).

3. R packages/functions

Use summary() for the complete fitted object; broom.mixed::tidy() for fixed/random parameters; emmeans for estimable means/trends/interaction contrasts; marginaleffects for response-scale standardization; VarCorr()/ranef() for variance components and BLUPs.

4. Data

MASS::epil is converted to a binary repeated outcome for a direct population-average versus subject-specific comparison.

data("epil", package = "MASS")
epil <- MASS::epil |>
  mutate(subject = factor(subject), period_c = period - 1, any_seizure = as.integer(y > 0)) |>
  arrange(subject, period)

5. Fit

if (requireNamespace("geepack", quietly = TRUE)) {
  gee_bin <- geepack::geeglm(
    any_seizure ~ trt * period_c + lbase + lage,
    id = subject, waves = period, data = epil,
    family = binomial, corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
}

glmm_bin <- glmer(
  any_seizure ~ trt * period_c + lbase + lage + (1 | subject),
  epil, family = binomial, nAGQ = 7
)

6. Extract & interpret

if (exists("gee_bin")) {
  cbind(estimate = coef(gee_bin), robust_se = sqrt(diag(gee_bin$geese$vbeta)))

Term: trt
Type: response
Comparison: progabide - placebo
Quantity Concise interpretation
LMM fixed intercept Expected response for the reference covariate pattern at the time origin; recenter time if this is extrapolative.
LMM fixed slope Expected response change per time unit for the reference group; with an interaction it is not the common slope.
Group x time Difference in time slopes (continuous time) or difference of occasion contrasts (factor time).
Random-intercept variance Residual between-subject heterogeneity in the conditional intercept.
Random-slope variance Residual between-subject heterogeneity in conditional change; marginal variance/correlation then depends on time.
Random-effect correlation Association between latent deviations; inspect time centering because it changes the intercept and its correlation with slope.
BLUP/conditional mode Shrunken subject deviation conditional on the fitted population model and variance parameters.
Random-intercept ICC \(\tau_0^2/(\tau_0^2+\sigma^2)\) for the Gaussian random-intercept model only.
GEE coefficient Population-average change in the link of the marginal mean.
GEE working \(\alpha\) Nuisance association parameter used for efficiency; not generally a target unless association is explicitly modeled.
GEE robust SE Sandwich uncertainty, asymptotically robust to working-correlation misspecification.
GEE model-based SE Valid only if the working covariance is correctly specified.
GEE scale \(\phi\) Marginal variance multiplier under the package’s scale-estimation rule.
Logistic GLMM \(e^{\beta}\) Subject-specific conditional odds ratio at equal random effects.
Logistic GEE \(e^{\beta}\) Population-average marginal odds ratio.
Poisson/log GLMM \(e^{\beta}\) Conditional rate ratio; an offset fixes the exposure denominator.
Satterthwaite/KR df Approximate denominator df for a specified fixed-effect test; KR also adjusts covariance/test statistic.

7. Diagnostics

Before interpreting, verify reference levels, time units/origin, contrast matrix, link/response scale, robust versus model-based covariance, convergence/singularity, dispersion, missing-data assumption, and whether predictions are conditional (re.form = NULL), random-effects-zero (re.form = NA), or marginalized/standardized.

contrasts(epil$trt)
          [,1]
placebo      1
progabide   -1
isSingular(glmm_bin)
[1] FALSE
glmm_bin@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages
NULL

8. Caveats

  • A main effect involved in an interaction is evaluated at the reference/zero value of the interacting variable.
  • re.form = NA in a nonlinear mixed model sets \(b=0\); it does not integrate over \(b\). Use marginal standardization or numerical integration for population-average predictions.
  • Odds ratios are noncollapsible; PA/SS differences can occur without confounding and are not explained solely by bias.
  • emmeans averages over the reference grid according to its weighting rule; state whether weights are equal, proportional, or standardized to a target population.
  • Report effect, scale, unit, contrast, uncertainty method, and multiplicity adjustment in the same sentence.
  • Source-backed: interpretation distinctions and attenuation follow BIOS 767/STAT 571. Standard-practice addition: marginaleffects gives explicit response-scale standardization.
